correctness.rationale: The quotient identity follows from the primitive-root argument and Gauss lemma. Its coefficients are partial sums of the periodic reciprocal of Φ_m. Each of the d blocks has nonempty support, by cyclotomic degree and monicity. Extending t by m inserts a complete cyclic support period in every block, fixes first/last support offsets at boundaries, and increments the gap multiset by exactly the sum of cyclic gap multisets. This proves the infinite affine law. At m=15 the displayed a- and u-vectors satisfy \(\Phi_{15}U_{15}=1-x^{15}\) exactly. An independent standard-library long-division checker validates every vector over 120 exhaustive parameter combinations (8 residues × 15 quotient values), polynomial-product tail coefficients, degree sums and lack of longer gaps; these calculations corroborate the finite table, not the general theorem.

originality.rationale: An implication-level comparison with full-text binary gap formulas, earlier ternary coefficient block formulas/table and the newer extremal gap theorem found none stating an exact affine all-length histogram for every odd squarefree cofactor or the full eight-class Φ15p table. Coefficient-block descriptions can reconstruct the polynomials and offer an implicit computational route, but published coefficient-value counts do not determine ordered gap frequencies; the explicit universal affine cyclic-gap law and four sharp support regimes are additional derived statements. A residual risk of implicit earlier coverage remains.
residual_risks: General coefficient block algorithms in earlier ternary literature may yield the affine histogram with additional unrecorded computations; lack of stated table does not logically prove novel independence.

value.rationale: The gap histogram retains adjacency information discarded by coefficient-value counts. Its exact affine dependence on the prime quotient is a structural all-cofactor phenomenon, and the complete Φ15p table determines four qualitatively different possible gap spectra, including the surprising exclusivity of gap length 6 to p≡±2 and of lengths 5 and 7 to p≡±1. This resolves a natural extension of recent binary gap-frequency results and is not a single isolated computed coefficient or a restatement of the known maximum-gap count. The universal finite cyclic formula makes further examples reproducible.
